Edward Gibbon, The History of the Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/edward-gibbon/the-history-of-the-decline-and-fall-of-the-roman-empire

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Edward Gibbon, the author, died 1794 (UK).

First publication of the text used: 1788 (SE colophon: 'published between 1776 and 1788' (latest volume 1788)).

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1788, before 1931;
  a published work enters the United States public domain 95 years after
  publication, so this work entered it in 1883.
- Country of origin (UK): copyright there lasts for life plus 70 years
  after the death of the last surviving person named above. The last to die
  did so in 1794, so the work entered the public domain there on
  1 January 1865.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."

Sources of these facts:
- Given repo slug does not exist; the actual SE repo is edward-gibbon_the-history-of-the-decline-and-fall-of-the-roman-empire (no various-translators suffix) and its colophon was used
- The actual colophon mentions no translator: Gibbon wrote in English, so the 'various translators' skip condition does not apply to the real edition
- SE colophon: published 1776-1788; no editor/introducer mentioned
- Wikidata Q161841 (Edward Gibbon, 'English historian and politician 1737-1794'), P570 = 1794-01-16 (famous item chosen)
